title: Shear faulting and localized heating in ice: The influence of confinement

nodes.label: Why ice under confinement switches between brittle-like and plastic shear faulting, and whether faults self-heat, is unexplained
Raising confinement suppresses frictional crack sliding, switching Coulombic to plastic faulting with localized heating
Freshwater granular and columnar (S2) ice as model polycrystals, grain size 1-8 mm
Confinement ratio R varied 0.1-0.5 along proportional triaxial paths; grain size varied
Thermistors frozen into specimens at fixed distances from the future fault record temperature in real time
Proportional triaxial compression at -10 C to terminal failure
Low-confinement C-fault: gouge of loose debris flanked by comb cracks, damage zone 2-3 grains wide
High-confinement P-fault: narrow band of fine recrystallized grains (50 um-0.5 mm), no gouge
Failure mode switches from Coulombic C-faulting (29 deg) to plastic P-faulting (42 deg) at R~0.3
Strength rises with confinement below R~0.3 and is confinement-independent (~23.5 MPa) above
C-fault strength scales with d^-1/2; P-fault strength is independent of grain size
C-faults are frictional Coulombic shear; P-faults follow the maximum-shear plane as pressure-insensitive plastic flow

attrs.mechanism_class: frictional sliding vs plastic shear localization

nodes.label: Localized plastic shear heats the band adiabatically, softening it and driving dynamic recrystallization
P-faults release far more localized heat than C-faults (frictional vs plastic heat generation)
Confinement selects the fault mechanism in ice: frictional C-faults below R~0.3, heat-generating plastic P-faults above
P-fault band contains ~50 um pores absent outside the fault, throughout the volume (micro-CT)
Coulomb shear faults form at ~30 deg to sigma1 (internal friction); plastic shear follows the 45 deg maximum-shear plane
Coulomb/Hall-Petch strength model (Eq. 2), C-P transition criterion (Eq. 8), heat conduction with fault heat sources (Eqs. 4-6)
Model strength curves, transition level and temperature histories agree with measurements
Low-R thin sections: conjugate faults ~60 deg apart, whitish gouge band, boxed comb cracks
